observations.content: Assistant confirmed no 'asker' agent was created from two spawn attempts that returned HTTP 202, concluding the 202 spawns genuinely failed rather than being slow successes.

Assistant's earlier probe create_agent got a validation error saying 'provider must be provider/model, for example codex/gpt-5.4', noting the daemon now requires the provider field as provider/model, possibly updated after a daemon restart at 12:34.
In extensions/subagent-types/paseo-spawn.ts line 90 sends provider: req.provider and line 67 types provider: string.
In extensions/subagent-types/index.ts line 246, providerStringFor(model, providerFamily='pi') returns model prefixed with providerFamily if not already prefixed.
Assistant determined the extension builds provider as pi/cli-openai/zaicp/glm-5.3-flash (4 segments) which worked this morning.

Direct curl create_agent with 4-segment provider pi/cli-openai/zaicp/glm-5.3-flash returned HTTP 200 and created agent 014ed15c-66f0-43f2-be5f-6af3d30438a3 (status running), proving the payload format is valid.
Respawn of 'asker' scout subagent via spawn_subagent failed again with 'Spawn failed: no MCP response (http 202)'.

Curl probe B with notifyOnFinish:true and provider pi/cli-openai/mmcp/MiniMax-M3 returned HTTP 200 and created agent fad4178d-9ded-49a1-851e-c025705a7732, which finished and replied PROBE_B_OK, so notifyOnFinish true is not the issue.

Raw Bun fetch (bun202.ts) using cfg from /tmp/paseo-pi-mcp-pJMw1M/mcp.json returned HTTP 200 and created agent c30ad572-bf1a-4dcf-ba30-4e3461e7988d which replied PROBE_C_OK, so Bun fetch is not the differentiator.

Running the extension's own code (importing findMcpEndpoint and createAgent from paseo-channel.ts) reproduced the failure: createAgent returned {ok:false, error:'no MCP response (http 202)'} while raw Bun fetch with identical args got 200.
The mcp.json URL and findMcpEndpoint-resolved URL are identical: http://127.0.0.1:6767/mcp/agents?callerAgentId=cf76ad71-3f82-4296-960f-fa9e2fcd06ee; token head fc0ec81f-51be-4c80-9.
Testing labels individually: subagent.role=scout returned 200 creating agent d8241d1d, subagent.parent=cf76ad71 returned 200 creating agent b0506df3, so subagent labels are not the cause.

Same-process pair test: raw fetch returned HTTP 200 (agent 48d2c58b created, replied PAIR_RAW_OK) while extension createAgent immediately after returned 202, proving the difference is inside the extension's mcpCall.
Reversed-order test: EXT-first createAgent call still returned 202 twice (pair2.ts), showing the 202 is deterministic inside mcpCall/createAgent, not a call-order or rate-limit effect.

A verbatim copy of mcpCall in a standalone script (same headers, body, signal) returned HTTP 200 and created agent 88f47bce, implying the live module's mcpCall differs from the dev copy that was read.

Each spawned agent got its own mcp.json in /tmp (t51cO0, FDGPGt, Dar20N, 1AWgLY, 912fH5, 4xQaXY, uKOpAX); only pJMw1M (12:34) has callerAgentId cf76ad71 matching the assistant's agent, so findMcpEndpoint resolves only pJMw1M.

Assistant temporarily patched live paseo-channel.ts mcpCall to log status/body under CHAN_DEBUG; the debug run showed [mcpCall] create_agent -> 202 with empty body, confirming the actual failing request returns 202 with an empty body.
